dossier.public_summary: The dip depth changes far too much between sectors and between individual transits (p=5e-8), including one transit that appears opposite in sign, inconsistent with a planet transit which should be stable. Centroiding is unavailable, but depth instability and low consistency strongly favor stellar variability or noise over a planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes wildly between sectors (1245 ppm in sector 7, 4391 ppm in sector 34, 9174 ppm in sector 61) with p_constant 5.221e-8 and chi2 33.54 dof 2, not a stable planet depth.
All data are the same product TESS-SPOC (depth 5513 ppm err 549 ppm p_constant 5.209660780405358e-08), so the 160.6% depth_change_pct changes within a source, not a calibration offset.
Individual transit depths are inconsistent at p 5.3803812529553295e-08, a single bad transit dominates the signal; this is positive evidence for spots, variability or a few bad events, not a planet.
reasons.value: p_consistent 5.3803812529553295e-08, top3 share 0.909, one transit -761 ppm sigma -4.2

reasons.why: Low planet score supports false positive; combined with stellar variability it favours a non-planet despite flat bottom (shape.v_sigma -1.643) and no secondary (secondary.snr 2.622) which alone would not earn gate2.
